eugs.question: What verification overhead did Pinocchio report for its evaluated applications?
eugs.answer_statement: For the evaluated Pinocchio system, proofs were 288 bytes and verification was typically about 10 ms; worker proof effort was reported as 19–60× lower than prior work.
eugs.boundary: Protocol-, implementation- and workload-specific measurements. No universal cheap/fast-verification claim.

eugs.question: What normal-case overhead did the reported Byzantine-fault-tolerant NFS implementation show versus standard NFS?
eugs.answer_statement: On the reported Andrew benchmark, the Byzantine-fault-tolerant NFS service took about 3% more time than standard unreplicated NFS.
eugs.boundary: Old, workload- and implementation-specific NFS benchmark; does not predict modern decentralized-compute overhead.
